trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Barcelona El Prat Airport at 19:20. Take the L9 Sud metro line to Torrassa, then transfer to reach Sant Just Desvern area (budget option ~€5.15 with T-Casual card). Check in to Sercotel Porta Barcelona. Once settled, take a short stroll around the local neighbourhood to get oriented and grab a light bite nearby.

meals.lunch: N/A – in transit or airport snack
meals.dinner: Bar/restaurant near the hotel in Sant Just Desvern – look for a local 'menú del día' or a neighbourhood tapas bar. Budget ~€8–12 for a simple set meal or bocadillo with a drink.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a T-Casual 10-trip metro card (€11.35) at the airport – it will save money throughout the trip. Keep the first evening light as it will be a long travel day. Temperatures around 28°C in the evening so dress light.

day_by_day.morning: Early breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café, then head into central Barcelona via metro. Start with the Gothic Quarter Architecture Walk – a self-guided tour through Barri Gòtic discovering Roman ruins, medieval palaces, the Barcelona Cathedral, Plaça Reial, and hidden alleyways. Pick up a free map at the tourist office or use a free app like Google Maps with offline mode. This is completely free and best enjoyed in the cooler morning hours (9:00–12:00).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk from the Gothic Quarter along La Rambla to the waterfront (La Barceloneta). Cool off with a dip at Barceloneta Beach (free). Explore the Port Olímpic area on foot. Grab lunch at a local chiringuito or a supermarket (Mercadona/Lidl) for a budget picnic on the beach. Rest during the hottest part of the day (14:00–16:00). In the late afternoon, visit the free exterior of the Palau de la Música Catalana and wander El Born neighbourhood.
day_by_day.evening: Head to El Born or the Gothic Quarter for pre-dinner drinks. Many bars offer free tapas with a drink during happy hour (18:00–20:00). Dinner in El Born, then explore the neighbourhood's bar scene – Bar del Pla and El Xampanyet are local favourites. The area comes alive after 22:00 for nightlife.

meals.breakfast: Café con leche and a croissant or tostada at a local café near the hotel – budget ~€3–4
meals.lunch: Supermarket picnic on Barceloneta Beach or a bocadillo from a local bakery – budget ~€5–7
meals.dinner: Set menú del día or tapas in El Born neighbourhood – budget ~€10–14. Try Bar del Pla for affordable Catalan tapas.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes – the Gothic Quarter has uneven cobblestones. Carry a refillable water bottle; public drinking fountains are available throughout the city. Sun protection is essential at 28°C+.

day_by_day.morning: Book the Sagrada Família Guided Tour in advance online (cheaper than at the door; standard entry ~€26, with tower access ~€36). Arrive at opening time (9:00) to beat the crowds. The guided tour with tower access offers panoramic views of the city and an in-depth look at Gaudí's architectural genius. Allow 2–2.5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Sagrada Família, walk or take the metro to Gràcia neighbourhood. Explore the free exterior of Casa Batlló and Casa Milà (La Pedrera) along Passeig de Gràcia – the 'Block of Discord' is a free architecture feast from the outside. Walk up to Parc Güell: the monumental zone requires a ticket (~€10, book online), but the surrounding park and viewpoints are free and offer stunning city views. Spend the hottest hours (14:00–17:00) resting in the shaded park areas.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Gràcia neighbourhood for the evening – it has a vibrant local nightlife scene with many affordable bars and terraces. Vermouth hour ('vermut') starts around 19:00. After dinner, explore the lively squares like Plaça del Sol and Plaça de la Vila de Gràcia, which fill with locals socialising well into the night.

meals.breakfast: Grab a pastry and coffee at a bakery near the hotel before heading out – budget ~€3–4
meals.lunch: Picnic in Parc Güell with supermarket supplies, or a budget bocadillo from a nearby café in Gràcia – budget ~€5–8
meals.dinner: Affordable tapas or a menú del día in Gràcia – try La Pepita or a local neighbourhood restaurant. Budget ~€10–14.

day_by_day.notes: Book Sagrada Família tickets at least a few days in advance – they sell out fast, especially in August. Book Parc Güell monumental zone tickets online too (~€10). Total architecture spend today ~€36–46 but these are the trip highlights worth the splurge.

day_by_day.morning: Visit La Boqueria Market on La Rambla (free entry) – best visited early (9:00–10:30) before the tourist crowds. Browse the colourful stalls of fresh produce, cured meats, and local specialities. Pick up affordable fresh fruit and snacks. Afterwards, explore the nearby MACBA (Museum of Contemporary Art) – the building's architecture by Richard Meier is striking and free to admire from outside. The surrounding Raval neighbourhood has excellent street art worth exploring.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the metro or a leisurely walk to Montjuïc. Ride the Telefèric de Montjuïc cable car (€12.70 return) for panoramic views, or hike up for free via the park paths. Visit the free exterior of the Castell de Montjuïc and enjoy the gardens. The Fundació Joan Miró is nearby (~€14 entry) if budget allows, or simply enjoy the free Jardins de Laribal and city views. Return to the city in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Barceloneta and Port Olímpic area for sunset over the Mediterranean. This is a great nightlife hub – Port Olímpic has numerous clubs and bars that get busy after 23:00. For a more local and affordable experience, try the bars along Carrer del Parlament in Sant Antoni neighbourhood, which has a trendy but budget-friendly bar scene.

meals.breakfast: Fresh fruit and a snack from La Boqueria Market – budget ~€4–6
meals.lunch: Affordable lunch in El Raval – try a menú del día at a local restaurant (many offer €10–12 three-course lunches with wine). Alternatively, a falafel wrap from one of the many Middle Eastern spots in Raval for ~€5.
meals.dinner: Tapas and drinks in Sant Antoni neighbourhood – Bar Calders or similar local spots. Budget ~€10–13.

day_by_day.notes: La Boqueria can be very touristy and overpriced for eating – stick to buying fresh produce rather than prepared food. The Montjuïc area is large; wear comfortable shoes. August evenings are warm so outdoor terraces are perfect for nightlife.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Eixample district on foot – a grid-planned neighbourhood showcasing Barcelona's modernista architecture. Walk along Passeig de Gràcia and spot the free exteriors of Casa Amatller, Casa Lleó Morera, and revisit Casa Batlló and La Pedrera from the outside. Pop into the Mercat de l'Abaceria in Gràcia (free entry) for a local market experience. Visit the free Jardins de la Ciutadella park – a beautiful green space with a lake, fountains, and the impressive Cascada Monumental.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the final afternoon at Barceloneta Beach for a last swim and relaxation. Walk along the Passeig Marítim promenade. Visit the free Barceloneta neighbourhood and its narrow streets. Do any last-minute souvenir shopping at affordable spots – avoid La Rambla tourist shops; instead try local shops in El Born or Gràcia for better prices and authentic items. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Barcelona – treat yourself to a slightly nicer meal within budget. Head back to the hotel and prepare luggage for the return journey. If the flight is not early the next morning, enjoy a final stroll in the local Sant Just Desvern area or a quiet drink at a neighbourhood bar.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast if included, or a café con leche and tostada con tomate at a local café – budget ~€3–5. Tostada con tomate (bread rubbed with tomato and olive oil) is a quintessential Catalan breakfast.
meals.lunch: Picnic in Parc de la Ciutadella with supplies from a local supermarket – budget ~€5–7
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on a final dinner – try a traditional Catalan restaurant in El Born or Barceloneta for paella or fideuà. Budget ~€15–20 for a special farewell meal.

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if needed for the afternoon. Keep metro T-Casual card topped up for airport transfer. Total estimated daily spend (excluding accommodation): Day 1 ~€15, Day 2 ~€30, Day 3 ~€55–65, Day 4 ~€40–50, Day 5 ~€30–40. Overall trip budget estimate: ~€170–200 excluding flights and accommodation.

day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit. Flight lands at El Prat Airport at 19:20. Take the Aerobus or a taxi (~25 min) to Sercotel Porta Barcelona in Sant Just Desvern. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into the hotel and take a relaxed stroll around Sant Just Desvern to get your bearings. Find a nearby local bar for a welcome drink and light bite – the neighborhood has several casual tapas spots along Carrer de la Generalitat.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Bar Restaurante local near the hotel – try a simple menú del día or pintxos and a glass of cava to kick off the trip. Budget ~€15–20 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Do not schedule anything before 19:20. The hotel is in Sant Just Desvern, about 8 km southwest of central Barcelona – reachable by bus (L60/L62) or taxi. Keep Day 1 light; jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Confirm hotel check-in time in advance. August evenings are warm (~22–24°C), so light clothing is fine.

day_by_day.morning: Sagrada Família Guided Tour (09:00–11:30): Head into Barcelona via bus or metro (L5, Sagrada Família stop). Join the skip-the-line guided tour of Gaudí's iconic basilica, including tower access for panoramic views over the city. Book tickets in advance online – tower slots fill up fast, especially in August. Arrive early to beat the heat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gothic Quarter Architecture Walk (12:30–15:30): After lunch, make your way to the Barri Gòtic for a self-guided or small-group walking tour. Discover Roman ruins beneath the city, medieval palaces, the Barcelona Cathedral, Plaça Reial, and hidden alleyways. Pick up a free map at the tourist office or use a guided audio app. The shaded narrow streets offer welcome relief from the August heat.
day_by_day.evening: Tapas Crawl on Carrer del Parlament (19:30–22:30): Head to the vibrant Sant Antoni neighborhood for a classic Barcelona tapas crawl. Graze through multiple bars sampling patatas bravas, jamón ibérico, croquetas, and fresh seafood. The area buzzes with locals and travelers alike – perfect for soaking up the city's social energy.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby café – try a croissant and café amb llet (coffee with milk). Budget ~€5–8.
meals.lunch: Bar/restaurant near the Gothic Quarter – look for a menú del día (starter, main, dessert, drink) for ~€12–15. Try La Plata or a similar traditional Catalan spot.
meals.dinner: Tapas crawl on Carrer del Parlament – budget ~€20–30 per person across 3–4 stops including drinks.

day_by_day.notes: August heat peaks around 28–30°C in the afternoon – carry water and wear sunscreen. The Sagrada Família is extremely popular; pre-booking is essential. Gothic Quarter is best explored on foot; wear comfortable shoes. Sant Antoni is lively until late – a great preview of Barcelona's nightlife culture.

day_by_day.morning: Park Güell & Gràcia Neighborhood (09:30–12:00): Visit Gaudí's whimsical Park Güell early to avoid crowds and heat. Book the Monumental Zone ticket in advance. After exploring the mosaic terraces and gingerbread gatehouses, wander down into the charming Gràcia neighborhood – browse its bohemian squares like Plaça del Sol and Plaça de la Vila de Gràcia.
day_by_day.afternoon: Palau de la Música Catalana Daytime Visit & Eixample Modernisme Walk (13:30–17:00): Head to the Palau de la Música Catalana for a guided daytime tour of this UNESCO-listed Modernista gem by Lluís Domènech i Montaner – a stunning complement to the Sagrada Família. Afterward, stroll the Eixample grid to spot other Modernista gems: Casa Batlló, Casa Milà (La Pedrera), and Casa Amatller along the Manzana de la Discordia. Admire facades without necessarily paying entry to all.
day_by_day.evening: Palau de la Música Catalana Evening Concert (20:00–22:00): Return to the Palau de la Música Catalana for a live evening concert inside this breathtaking hall – the stained glass ceiling and sculpted interior are even more magical when lit up. Check the August concert schedule and book tickets in advance (~€30–50 depending on performance). A truly memorable Barcelona experience.

meals.breakfast: Café in Gràcia neighborhood – try a local bakery for pa amb tomàquet (bread with tomato) and coffee. Budget ~€5–7.
meals.lunch: Cervecería or casual restaurant in Eixample – try a set lunch menu near Passeig de Gràcia. Budget ~€14–18.
meals.dinner: Pre-concert dinner near Palau de la Música – El Xampanyet in El Born or a nearby bistro. Budget ~€20–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Park Güell timed entry is mandatory for the Monumental Zone – book online. The Palau de la Música concert schedule varies; check palaumusica.cat well in advance. Evening concerts typically start at 20:00 or 21:00. Dress smart-casual for the concert. This is a culturally rich day balancing architecture and live performance.

day_by_day.morning: Barceloneta Beach & Waterfront (09:00–12:00): Head to Barceloneta Beach for a morning swim before the crowds and heat peak. Walk along the Passeig Marítim, admire Frank Gehry's golden Fish sculpture, and explore the Port Olímpic marina area. The sea breeze makes mornings here very pleasant in August.
day_by_day.afternoon: El Born Cultural Quarter & Picasso Museum Area (13:00–17:00): Explore the El Born neighborhood – one of Barcelona's most stylish districts. Visit the Mercat de Santa Caterina (a colorful alternative to La Boqueria), browse independent boutiques, and consider a visit to the Picasso Museum (book online, ~€14). Wander the medieval streets and enjoy the architectural contrast between Gothic and contemporary design.
day_by_day.evening: Razzmatazz Club Night (00:00–04:00 into Aug 20): Ease into the evening with dinner and drinks in El Born or Eixample. Barcelona nightlife starts late – pre-drinks at a rooftop bar around 22:00, then head to Razzmatazz (Carrer dels Almogàvers, 122) after midnight. One of Europe's top clubs with five rooms spanning electronic, indie, and pop. Entry ~€15–20 including first drink.

meals.breakfast: Chiringuito (beach bar) at Barceloneta – fresh orange juice, tostada, and coffee. Budget ~€6–9.
meals.lunch: El Born neighborhood restaurant – try Bar del Pla or similar for Catalan cuisine. Budget ~€15–20.
meals.dinner: Pre-club dinner in Eixample or El Raval – a relaxed sit-down meal around 21:00. Try Parking Pizza or a mid-range Mediterranean spot. Budget ~€18–25.

day_by_day.notes: Razzmatazz doesn't get busy until 01:00–02:00 – this is normal for Barcelona. Buy tickets online in advance to avoid queues. Wear comfortable shoes you can dance in. Stay hydrated throughout the night. Plan to sleep in on Day 5 morning. Keep valuables secure in the club. Taxis back to Sant Just Desvern will be needed after the club (~€20–25 at that hour).

day_by_day.morning: Slow Morning & Montjuïc (11:00–13:00): After the late night, enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast and a slow start. Head to Montjuïc by cable car or funicular for sweeping views over the city and port. Visit the Fundació Joan Miró (one of Europe's finest modern art museums, ~€14) or simply enjoy the gardens and castle views without rushing.
day_by_day.afternoon: La Boqueria Market & Las Ramblas Final Stroll (14:30–17:30): Make your way to La Boqueria market on Las Ramblas for a final sensory Barcelona experience – fresh fruit, local cheeses, cured meats, and seafood. Browse rather than eat a full meal here (it's touristy but iconic). Walk the full length of Las Ramblas down to the Columbus Monument and the waterfront for a farewell look at the city.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner in Eixample or Sant Antoni (19:30–21:30): Enjoy a relaxed farewell dinner at a mid-range restaurant. Consider Bodega Sepúlveda or a similar Catalan wine bar in Sant Antoni for a final taste of local cuisine. Return to the hotel, pack, and prepare for departure.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast – take your time. Budget included in accommodation or ~€8–12 if external.
meals.lunch: Snacks and fresh fruit from La Boqueria market – budget ~€8–12 for a grazing lunch.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a mid-range Catalan restaurant – three courses with wine. Budget ~€25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Day 5 is intentionally relaxed to recover from the Razzmatazz night. Montjuïc is best visited mid-morning when it's not too hot. La Boqueria is very crowded in August – go with a browsing mindset rather than expecting a quiet meal. Confirm any departure logistics for the following day. Keep receipts for any VAT refund claims if applicable. Overall trip tip: an Hola BCN! travel card (3 or 5 days) covers metro, bus, and FGC trains and is excellent value for getting around the city from Sant Just Desvern.

day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Barcelona El Prat Airport at 19:20 on TAP Air Portugal. A pre-arranged private luxury transfer (Mercedes E-Class or similar) whisks you to Sercotel Porta Barcelona in Sant Just Desvern. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll around the quiet residential neighbourhood to decompress after the flight.

meals.dinner: Dinner at El Celler de Can Roca's sister concept or, closer to the hotel, reserve a table at Restaurante La Masia de Can Planes (Sant Just Desvern) – a charming Catalan farmhouse restaurant serving refined local cuisine with excellent natural wines. Alternatively, room service from the hotel for a relaxed first night.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Confirm your private driver in advance so there are no delays after landing. August evenings in Barcelona average around 24–26 °C – perfect for a short outdoor walk. Hydrate well after the flight.

day_by_day.morning: After a leisurely hotel breakfast, take a private car into central Barcelona (≈20 min). Begin the day with the Sagrada Família Guided Tour – skip-the-line entry with a knowledgeable guide, including tower access for sweeping panoramic views over the Eixample grid. Book the first entry slot (9:00 AM) to beat the August crowds and enjoy the morning light streaming through the stained-glass windows.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Palau de la Música Catalana for a self-guided or private guided architectural visit of the interior (separate from the evening concert). Afterwards, explore the El Born neighbourhood on foot – browse the Mercat de Santa Caterina, admire the colourful mosaic roof, and pop into boutique design shops. Relax with a cold drink at a terrace café before heading back to freshen up.
day_by_day.evening: Attend the Palau de la Música Catalana Evening Concert – a live performance inside this UNESCO-listed Modernista jewel designed by Lluís Domènech i Montaner. The combination of the ornate stained-glass skylight and world-class acoustics makes this an unmissable luxury cultural experience.

meals.breakfast: Full buffet breakfast at the hotel or a specialty coffee and pastry at a local café near the hotel.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Cervecería Catalana (Eixample) – beloved for its premium montaditos and fresh seafood, or upgrade to a tasting menu at Disfrutar (book well in advance), one of Barcelona's Michelin-starred gems near the Sagrada Família area.
meals.dinner: Pre-concert dinner at Casa Paloma or Llamber (El Born) – both offer refined Catalan-Mediterranean menus in elegant settings, ideal for a special evening before the concert.

day_by_day.notes: Book Sagrada Família tower access and the Palau concert tickets well in advance – both sell out weeks ahead in August. Dress smart-casual for the evening concert. Private car or taxi recommended between sites given the August heat.

day_by_day.morning: Embark on the Gothic Quarter Architecture Walk – join a small premium group tour or hire a private guide for a deep-dive through the Barri Gòtic. Discover Roman ruins beneath the city, the Barcelona Cathedral, Plaça Reial, and hidden medieval passages. A private guide elevates the experience with exclusive access and storytelling unavailable on standard tours.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the walk, cross into the Raval neighbourhood and visit the MACBA (Museum of Contemporary Art) or the CCCB for a cultural interlude. Then head to Montjuïc via the Telefèric cable car for sweeping city views. Explore the Fundació Joan Miró at a relaxed pace, enjoying the art and the hilltop breeze away from the city heat.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Barcelona's legendary nightlife at Razzmatazz – one of Europe's top clubs with five distinct rooms spanning electronic, indie, and pop music. Arrive around midnight (clubs in Barcelona don't peak until 1–2 AM). Arrange VIP table service in advance for the full luxury experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a visit to Federal Café (El Born) for avocado toast and specialty single-origin coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Bar del Pla (El Born) – a refined yet relaxed spot for Catalan classics like croquetas, anchovies, and fresh fish. Excellent natural wine list.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Tickets (Albert Adrià's avant-garde tapas bar, El Poble Sec) – a theatrical, Michelin-starred experience. Book months ahead. Alternatively, Bodega Sepúlveda for a more intimate wine-focused dinner before the late night out.

day_by_day.notes: Pace yourself for the late night at Razzmatazz – take a siesta in the late afternoon if needed. Pre-book VIP entry or table service directly through the club's website. Wear comfortable shoes for the Gothic Quarter walk on cobblestones. Stay hydrated throughout the day.

day_by_day.morning: A slower start after the late night. Sleep in and enjoy a late hotel breakfast. Mid-morning, take a private car to Park Güell for a premium guided tour of Gaudí's whimsical hilltop park – book the timed entry for the Monumental Zone. The elevated terraces offer spectacular views over Barcelona and the Mediterranean. Visit early enough to avoid peak midday heat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to the Gràcia neighbourhood for a leisurely afternoon. Explore the charming Plaça del Sol and Plaça de la Vila de Gràcia, browse independent boutiques, and visit the Casa Vicens (Gaudí's first major work, recently opened to the public) for another architectural gem. Enjoy a cold horchata or craft beer at a shaded terrace.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Barceloneta beachfront for a sunset aperitivo at a rooftop bar – Eclipse Bar at the W Barcelona Hotel offers one of the city's most spectacular sunset views over the Mediterranean. Afterwards, explore the vibrant Port Olímpic area or return to El Born for cocktails at a premium cocktail bar such as Paradiso (ranked among the world's best bars).

meals.breakfast: Late breakfast at the hotel – full buffet to recharge after the previous night.
meals.lunch: Lunch at La Pepita (Gràcia) – creative Catalan sandwiches and small plates in a beautifully tiled space, or upgrade to a set lunch menu at Botafumeiro for premium Galician seafood.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Enoteca Paco Pérez at the Hotel Arts Barcelona (Barceloneta) – a two-Michelin-starred seafood-focused tasting menu with Mediterranean views. One of Barcelona's finest dining experiences.

day_by_day.notes: Park Güell timed entry is mandatory for the Monumental Zone – book online in advance. The W Barcelona rooftop can get busy; consider a reservation. Paradiso cocktail bar has a queue system – arrive early or check for reservations.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning – enjoy a relaxed hotel breakfast and check out (or arrange a late check-out). Take a private car to the Passeig de Gràcia for a final architectural promenade: admire the Block of Discord featuring Casa Batlló and Casa Amatller side by side. If time allows, book a premium guided tour inside Casa Batlló (the 'Magic Nights' experience is spectacular if visiting in the evening, but the daytime tour with AR glasses is equally impressive).
day_by_day.afternoon: Indulge in a final luxury shopping session along Passeig de Gràcia and Avinguda Diagonal – home to flagship stores of Loewe, Hermès, and local Catalan designers. Alternatively, visit the Museu Nacional d'Art de Catalunya (MNAC) on Montjuïc for a final cultural flourish, with its breathtaking Romanesque art collection and panoramic terrace views.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell tapas crawl on Carrer del Parlament in the Sant Antoni neighbourhood – graze through the vibrant bar scene sampling patatas bravas, jamón ibérico, fresh anchovies, and Catalan craft beers or cava. This lively, local neighbourhood offers an authentic and festive send-off to Barcelona. End the night with a final cocktail at a rooftop bar before your private transfer back to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast – make it a full, leisurely affair on the last morning.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Bodega Sepúlveda or Quimet & Quimet (Poble Sec) – a legendary standing-room-only bodega famous for its creative montaditos and tinned seafood. A true Barcelona institution.
meals.dinner: Tapas crawl on Carrer del Parlament – Bar Calders, Federal, and Morro Fi are premium stops. Budget €40–60 per person for a full grazing experience with drinks.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange your departure transfer in advance. Sant Antoni's tapas scene is best enjoyed from 20:00 onwards when locals fill the terraces. August evenings are warm and lively – perfect for an outdoor farewell dinner. Keep some euros in cash as some smaller tapas bars are cash-only.

query: Barcelona architecture and nightlife, $2000, 5 days, August from NYC
